# CVR Engineering — Phase 1 Baseline: Findings

**Deliverable:** `model/CVR_Model_Phase1_Baseline.xlsx` (generated by `scripts/build_phase1_workbook.py`)
**Sources:** 2026 rate sheet · CVR/EPC KPI report (7/11/2026) · **GL financial statements through 6/30/2026** — all in `data/`
**Status:** v2 — GL statements incorporated; most finance open items now answered from source

---

## What the workbook contains

| Tab | Contents |
|---|---|
| README | Purpose, color key, sources |
| Assumptions | Global inputs; overhead, interest, and burden now GL-sourced |
| Rates | The 2026 rate card and billing policies |
| Roster & Hours | 13 people, YTD hours, utilization vs targets, billable value at card rates |
| Baseline P&L | CVR monthly actuals vs budget, **Jan–Jun 2026** (Jan–May per KPI report, June per GL) |
| GL Income Stmt | Full line-item income statement (June + YTD, actual/budget/prior year) with computed OILI |
| Balance Sheet | 6/30/2026 vs one year ago vs budget |
| Cash Flow & Customers | Six-month cash flow and sales by customer with intercompany split |
| HWC EPC Baseline | EPC line context |
| Realization | $/hr gap analysis, labor-multiplier view, utilization × realization grid |
| Checks & Open Items | Ten automatic tie-outs across all three sources |

The two data sources cross-tie exactly: GL YTD-June minus GL June equals the KPI report's Jan–May figures for revenue, GP, and net income — both sources are describing the same books.

## Findings

**1. Realization is ~79% — realized rate $122/hr against a $154/hr blended card.** With the GL period (June 30) much closer to the hours window (July 11), the timing noise shrinks: ~4,505 billable hours × $154.47 card = $695.8K of value vs $551.0K recognized — a **~$145K gap**. Intercompany pricing is the lead suspect: the GL confirms CVR's hours on Hydaker-Wheatlake jobs **are** revenue-credited as intercompany sales (~20% of YTD revenue), so the open question is whether that work bills at the standard card or a discounted schedule.

**2. The labor multiplier tells the loss-leader story in one number: actual 1.29x vs budget 2.60x.** CVR earns $1.29 of revenue per direct-labor dollar; the budget (and healthy engineering firms, typically 2.5–3.0x) expects roughly double. Direct labor is running at ~$95/hr per billable hour against $122/hr realized. Splitting the fix between price (realization) and cost (who is charging time to jobs, at what pay) needs the salary detail — the last major finance ask.

**3. The GL answers most Phase 1 finance questions:**
- **Corporate overhead allocation:** $17,250/month flat ($103.5K YTD), identical in budget — a fixed, predictable driver.
- **Interest:** ~$5K/month accruing on a **$3.44M Note Payable-Parent**; not in budget, so OILI trails budget by ~$60K/yr even at budgeted operating performance.
- **Employment burden:** ~33.8% of total wages (FICA, UI, WC, health, pension, benefits, vac/holiday), computed from GL lines.
- **Subcontract:** zero in 2026 (prior year carried $218K of subcontract cost at a −70% gross margin — that bleed has already been stopped).

**4. The balance sheet quantifies the loss-leader history: equity is −$3.35M.** CVR holds no cash and no fixed assets — it is essentially a $140K AR balance funded by the parent note, which absorbed another $477K in H1. The cumulative deficit is the baseline the turnaround gets measured against. AR tripled year-over-year ($46K → $140K), consistent with growing external billing.

**5. June was the best month of the year** — $124.4K revenue (still 26% under budget), 36.8% gross margin, and a near-breakeven operating result (−$9.8K before interest). Prior-year June lost $85K. The trajectory is real; the budget's full-year +$139.4K net income still requires a strong H2.

**6. Customer mix confirmed in dollars:** CenterPoint 69.7% of revenue, intercompany HWC work 20.2%, all other external customers ~10% combined. Revenue concentration matches the hours concentration seen in the KPI report.

## Remaining Phase 1 exit items

1. **Salaries by person** — the one remaining finance ask; splits the 1.29x-vs-2.60x multiplier gap into price vs cost.
2. Explain June's negative Labor-Indirect (−$6,078) — reclass or credit?
3. Confirm the intercompany rate schedule for HWC work (standard card vs discounted).
4. Confirm classifications: Taylor Nelson, Kevin Metts (not on org chart); VP time billing class; where Tom Little / Erin Bryden / Patrick Nicholson book their time.
5. Decompose the ~$145K realization gap on the Realization tab once the above land.
